source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 171: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: treat a calculator call as unnecessary only when the operation, operands, units, and required precision are fully determined and safely answerable without external computation; otherwise classify the case as tool-required or ambiguous and clarify rather than guess. Falsifiable hypothesis: on a preregistered, held-out, stratified set of known-answer, tool-required, ambiguous, malformed, adversarial, and injected-failure tasks, a typed stop/no-tool gate will reduce unnecessary-call rate, median trajectory length, and calculator latency/cost, while the 95% confidence lower bound for final correctness is within a 1 percentage-point non-inferiority margin of the ungated baseline. Intervention: choose among stop/answer, calculator-needed, and clarify; require a parseable expression plus unit and precision checks; cap retries at two; validate tool syntax, units, range, and consistency; and on timeout, malformed, duplicate, wrong, unavailable, inconsistent, or unauthorized output return uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of fabricating a result. Measure per request and by slice: unnecessary-call rate, justified-call recall, tool success and validation failure, final correctness, trajectory length, recovery rate, latency in milliseconds, cost, abstention, and retry-loop rate. Use randomized paired evaluation with disjoint tuning data, blinded correctness adjudication, bootstrap confidence intervals, and logs of task mix, arithmetic magnitude, load, model version, tool version, and failures. Test no-tool, tool-required, ambiguity, precision-boundary, timeout, malformed, wrong-result, duplicate, adversarial, permission, and retry-loop cases. Use preference/reward shaping only as a capped secondary signal; guard against unsafe abstention and reward hacking. Canary the gate, monitor correctness and missed-tool slices, and roll back if correctness, justified-call recall, safety, or error/latency thresholds regress. Minimize prompt and tool-log retention, enforce authorization, and obtain domain-expert review before treating results as authoritative. Variant 171 is an input stratum, not evidence of the hypothesis.

Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: treat a calculator call as unnecessary only when the operation, operands, units, and required precision are fully determined and safely answerable without external computation; otherwise classify the case as tool-required or ambiguous and clarify rather than guess. Falsifiable hypothesis: on a preregistered, held-out, stratified set of known-answer, tool-required, ambiguous, malformed, adversarial, and injected-failure tasks, a typed stop/no-tool gate will reduce unnecessary-call rate, median trajectory length, and calculator latency/cost, while the 95% confidence lower bound for final correctness is within a 1 percentage-point non-inferiority margin of the ungated baseline. Intervention: choose among stop/answer, calculator-needed, and clarify; require a parseable expression plus unit and precision checks; cap retries at two; validate tool syntax, units, range, and consistency; and on timeout, malformed, duplicate, wrong, unavailable, inconsistent, or unauthorized output return uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of fabricating a result. Measure per request and by slice: unnecessary-call rate, justified-call recall, tool success and validation failure, final correctness, trajectory length, recovery rate, latency in milliseconds, cost, abstention, and retry-loop rate. Use randomized paired evaluation with disjoint tuning data, blinded correctness adjudication, bootstrap confidence intervals, and logs of task mix, arithmetic magnitude, load, model version, tool version, and failures. Test no-tool, tool-required, ambiguity, precision-boundary, timeout, malformed, wrong-result, duplicate, adversarial, permission, and retry-loop cases. Use preference/reward shaping only as a capped secondary signal; guard against unsafe abstention and reward hacking. Canary the gate, monitor correctness and missed-tool slices, and roll back if correctness, justified-call recall, safety, or error/latency thresholds regress. Minimize prompt and tool-log retention, enforce authorization, and obtain domain-expert review before treating results as authoritative. Variant 181 is an input stratum, not evidence of the hypothesis.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers assumptions, mechanism, explicit hypothesis, metrics, controlled evaluation, confounders, failure modes, reward safeguards, rollback, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.correctness: rewrite: separates unnecessary, justified, and ambiguous calculator use and preserves final correctness as a guardrail
quality_dimensions.measurement: per-request and sliced rates, correctness, recovery, latency in milliseconds, cost, and retry telemetry with uncertainty intervals
quality_dimensions.robustness: tests malformed, wrong, duplicate, timeout, unavailable, unauthorized, adversarial, precision-boundary, and retry-loop cases
quality_dimensions.evidence: requires preregistration, randomized paired held-out evaluation, disjoint tuning, adjudication, privacy review, and expert review

risks: The 1 percentage-point margin and retry cap are design choices requiring empirical validation.
Task difficulty, arithmetic magnitude, prompt mix, model/tool versions, and load may confound comparisons.
Rewarding fewer calls can cause unsafe abstention, missed tool-required work, or reward hacking; monitor slices and cap the signal.
Prompts and tool traces may contain sensitive data; minimize retention and enforce authorization.
evidence_required: Preregistered taxonomy and held-out randomized paired results with confidence intervals.
Independent correctness and justified-call adjudication including boundary and adversarial slices.
Trace-level latency, cost, error, and recovery telemetry with privacy review.
Canary thresholds and rollback drill results plus domain-expert review before authoritative use.
